text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former interior minister Meral Aksener says at a news conference on a spying scandal that an illegal grouping has been formed in the military.
- A high-ranking general says Aksener's statement alleging that she prevented a military coup is nonsense.
- A deputy chairman of the conservative True Path Party (DYP) resigns from the party, reducing its seats in parliament to 101.
- The new government will abolish a compulsory savings scheme directed at employees and employers.
- The state minister responsible for the economy says 100,000 cattle will be given free to locals in the impoverished east and southeast of Turkey.
- A Turkish court turns down a request to annul a court decision freezing accounts and securities of the Islamist group Kombassan.
- High-ranking police official Hanefi Avci says a security scandal which erupted in November, revealing ties between the state and the underworld, has been neglected.
- A volunteer women's organisation opens a free summer school for poor students in the Kadikoy district of Istanbul.
- A Coopers & Lybrand study reveals that managers received a pay rise of around 40-45 percent in the first half of 1997.
- The education ministry seeks financial resources to put an eight-year compulsory education plan into practice.
- A $500-million project to turn a demilitarised zone near the border with Greece into a holiday resort is under preparation.
